current.text: Monk is projected to come off the bench as the backup point guard behind Acuff and LaVine.
Last season Sacramento gave him DNPs and low minutes and at times left him out of the rotation.
Experts think coach Doug Christie, the front office and the team dislike him, and he could get DNPs again.
He is not expected to get back to a 29-minute role. At 27 minutes a night he would be rostered in every league.
Experts see him as an option only in 14 to 16 team leagues. They do not trust Sacramento to give him a big enough bench role, so they say do not draft him.
Sacramento could give bench minutes to Nique Clifford instead of him.
Trade rumors about him continue. He has 2 years left on his contract, including a player option.
The Kings are projected near the bottom of the league, and poor coaching, ownership and front office make their rotations unpredictable.

durable.text: He does not play defense and cannot hold up defensively for heavy minutes.
Experts rate him as a really good player when he gets minutes.

note: Both sites value Monk at 0 USD (Yahoo rank 222, ESPN rank 161), and he went for 2 USD in our league last season. That puts him outside our 144-player draft pool, and the experts say do not draft him in a 12-team league. His FT% and threes help a little and no category is flagged weak, but a bench role close to last season's 22 minutes gives too little volume. Early in the season, watch whether Sacramento gives him about 27 minutes a night. If it does, he becomes a waiver add.
